source_text:
Ἀκτημοσύνη,
φιλαργυρίας ἐκρίζωμα, ἀφιλαργυρίας δὲ ῥίζωμα, καρπὸς ἀγάπης, καὶ σταυρὸς ζωῆς, ἀνώδυνος βίος, ἀνεπίφθονος θησαυρὸς, ἀμέριμνος οὐρανὸς, ἀπερίσπαστος ἥλιος, ἀμέτρητος ὕλη, ἀκατάληπτος πλοῦτος, μερίμνης δρέπανον, Εὐαγγελίων πρᾶξις, ἄλυτος κόσμος. ὀξύδρομος ἀγωνιστής. Λύπη, ζημίας ἔνοικος, ἀποτυχίας συνόμιλος, ξενιτείας πρόδρομος, συγγενείας μνήμη, στενώσεως πάρεδρος, ἀκηδίας σύμφοιτος, παροξυσμοῦ ἔγκλημα, ὕβρεως ὑπόμνημα, καὶ ψυχῆς σκότισμα, ἠθῶν κατήφεια, φρονήσεως μέθη, ὑπνω 79.1144 τικὸν ἀντίδοτον, μορφῆς νέφος, σαρκὸς σκώληξ, λογισμῶν λύπη, αἰχμαλωσίας δῆμος. Χαρὰ, λύπης ὄλεθρος, καὶ συμφορῶν εὐχαριστία, εὐχῶν ὀπτασία. καὶ πόνων εὐφρασία, εὐποιΐας ἱλαρότης, ἀποταγῆς ἔνθεμα, φιλοξενίας δοχεῖον, ἐλπίδων καταφυγὴ, ἀσκούντων τροφὴ, πενθούντων παραίνεσις, δακρύων παρηγορία, θλίψεως ἀντίληψις, ἀγάπης ἔμψηφος, καὶ μακροθυμίας σύμψηφος. Ὀργὴ, φρονήσεως διαρπαγὴ, καταστάσεως ἀνασκευὴ, φύσεως σύγχυσις, ἠγριωμένη μορφὴ, κάμινος καρδίας, ἐρευγομένη φλὸξ, θυμοῦ νόμος, ὕβρεων μῆνις, μήτηρ θηρίων, σιωπῶσα μάχη, εὐχῆς σκῶλον. Μακροθυμία, φρονήσεως ὅπλον, ὀργῆς δικαστήριον καρδίας, ἰατρεῖον, θρασυνομένων νουθεσία, ταρασσομένων γαλήνη, ἀχείμαστος λιμὴν, λυποῦσιν εὐποιΐα, πρὸς πάντας ἠπιότης, βλασφημουμένη εὐλογεῖ, ὑβριζομένη ἀγάλλεται, στενουμένων παραμύθιον, ἐλπιζομένων ἔσοπτρον, κακουχουμένων βραβεῖον. ΚΕΦΑΛ. ∆ʹ.
orientation: Evagrius continues his catalogue of the eight principal vices and their opposing virtues, now giving the epithet-chains for poverty, grief, joy, anger, and patience.
pass_a_gloss: Poverty, a root-cutting of love of money, and a root of freedom from love of money, a fruit of love, and a cross of life, a painless life, an envy-free treasure, a carefree heaven, an undistracted sun, a measureless matter, an incomprehensible wealth, a sickle of care, a doing of the Gospels, an indissoluble order. A swift-running contestant. Grief, a dweller in loss, a companion of failure, a forerunner of exile, a memory of kinship, an assessor of straitness, a fellow traveler of listlessness, a charge of provocation, a reminder of insult, and a darkening of soul, a downcastness of habits, a drunkenness of prudence, a sleep-inducing antidote, a cloud of form, a worm of flesh, a grief of thoughts, a people of captivity. Joy, a destruction of grief, and a thanksgiving of misfortunes, a vision of prayers, and a gladness of labors, a cheerfulness of doing good, a planting of renunciation, a vessel of hospitality, a refuge of hopes, a food of ascetics, an exhortation of mourners, a consolation of tears, a help of affliction, a voter for love, and a fellow voter for patience. Anger, a plundering of prudence, an overturning of state, a confusion of nature, a wild form, a furnace of heart, a belching flame, a law of wrath, a rage of insults, a mother of beasts, a silent battle, a thorn of prayer. Patience, a weapon of prudence, a court of anger, a hospital of heart, an admonition of the bold, a calm of the troubled, a stormless harbor, a doing good to those who grieve, a gentleness toward all, when blasphemed it blesses, when insulted it exults, a comfort of the straitened, a mirror of those who hope, a prize of those who are ill-treated. CHAPTER 4.

choices.why: The noun denotes the act or result of uprooting; rendering it as 'root-cutting' preserves the active, destructive force against love of money, matching the parallel 'root' (ῥίζωμα) for the virtue.
The adjective means 'not subject to envy' or 'not attracting envy'; 'envy-free' keeps the privative alpha visible and ties to the vice of envy (φθόνος) in the treatise.
The adjective means 'free from care' (μέριμνα); 'carefree' is the most literal English equivalent and preserves the link to 'care' (μέριμνα) later in the chain.
The adjective means 'not drawn away' or 'not distracted'; 'undistracted' is the standard literal rendering and fits the monastic ideal of freedom from distraction.
The compound means 'swift-running'; 'contestant' (ἀγωνιστής) is the literal term for one who competes in a contest, preserving the athletic imagery.
The adjective means 'having a vote' or 'voting'; rendering it as 'a voter for' preserves the political/judicial metaphor and the parallel with 'fellow voter' (σύμψηφος).

pass_b_english: Poverty is the uprooting of love of money and the root of freedom from love of money. It is the fruit of love and a cross of life. It is a life without pain, a treasure free from envy, a heaven free from care, a sun that is never distracted, matter without measure, wealth beyond comprehension. It is a sickle for worry, a doing of the Gospels, a world that cannot be dissolved, a swift-footed athlete.

Grief lives with loss and keeps company with failure. It runs ahead of exile, remembers one's family, sits beside hardship, and travels with listlessness. It is an accusation of irritation, a reminder of insult, and a darkening of the soul. It is a downcastness of character, a drunkenness of prudence, a sleep-inducing antidote, a cloud over one's form, a worm of the flesh, a grief of thoughts, and a populace of captivity.

Joy is the destruction of grief and thanksgiving in misfortunes. It is a vision of prayers and gladness in labors, a cheerfulness in doing good, a planting of renunciation, a vessel of hospitality, a refuge of hopes, food for those in training, encouragement for those who mourn, comfort for tears, help in affliction. It is in agreement with love and of one mind with patience.

Anger is a plundering of prudence, an overturning of one's settled state, a confusion of nature, a wild appearance, a furnace of the heart, a belching flame, a law of fury, a wrath of insults, a mother of wild beasts, a silent battle, and a thorn in prayer.

Patience is a weapon of prudence, a courtroom for anger, and a place of healing for the heart, an admonition to the reckless, a calm for the troubled, a harbor without storms. It does good to those who cause grief, is gentle toward everyone, blesses when blasphemed, rejoices when insulted, is a comfort to the distressed, a mirror of the things hoped for, and a prize for those who suffer hardship.
notes: The source contains 'ὑπνω 79.1144 τικὸν' with a page/column number '79.1144' inserted mid-word; the word is read as ὑπνωτικὸν ('sleep-inducing').

problems.quote: Poverty cuts out the root of love of money
problems.why: Source says poverty *is* the root of love of money, not that it cuts it out.
problems.fix: Poverty is the root of love of money
problems.ruling: ἐκρίζωμα means 'uprooting/removal,' not 'root'; poverty IS the uprooting, not that it cuts it out.
σύμψηφος = 'voting together with,' but context demands 'fellow-voter/elector with'; 'votes together' is awkward and misleading.

edits.old: Poverty cuts out the root of love of money
edits.new: Poverty is the root of love of money

edits.old: It votes for love and votes together with patience.
edits.new: It is radiant with love and shines together with patience.

fixed: Changed 'cuts out the root' to 'is the root' because the source says poverty *is* the root of love of money (φιλαργυρίας ἐκρίζωμα), not that it cuts it out.
Changed 'votes for love' to 'radiant with love' because ἔμψηφος means 'shining, radiant,' not 'votes.'
Changed 'votes together with patience' to 'shines together with patience' because σύμψηφος means 'shining together,' not 'votes together.'

problems.why: Greek describes a “sharp‑spirited fighter” or “fierce combatant”, not a “swift‑running contestant”.

problems.quote: Poverty is the root of love of money and is itself the root of freedom from love of money
problems.source_quote: Ἀκτημοσύνη, φιλαργυρίας ἐκρίζωμα, ἀφιλαργυρίας δὲ ῥίζωμα
problems.why: Reverses the roots: source says poverty is uprooting of love of money, root of freedom from love of money
problems.fix: Poverty is the uprooting of love of money and the root of freedom from love of money
problems.ruling: Source says poverty is the uprooting (ἐκρίζωμα) of love of money and root (ῥίζωμα) of anti‑love; translation reverses.

problems.quote: radiant with love and shines together with patience
problems.why: ἔμψηφος and σύμψηφος mean 'voting with/assenting to', not 'radiant with' and 'shines together with'; joy votes with love and patience
problems.fix: casting its vote with love and sharing its vote with patience
problems.ruling: ἔμψηφος, σύμψηφος derive from ψῆφος ‘vote’; they mean ‘in accord with’, not ‘radiant/shining with’.

problems.quote: It does good to those who grieve it
problems.why: λυποῦσιν is dative plural 'to those who cause grief/annoyance', not 'those who grieve it' (passive); patience does good to those who cause it grief
problems.fix: It does good to those who grieve it
problems.ruling: λυποῦσιν takes dative; εὐποιΐα is dative ‘to good deeds’, so ‘they cause grief to good deeds’, not ‘does good to those who grieve it’.

problems.why: Greek says “inexhaustible treasure”; English adds “no one envies”, a meaning not in the source.
problems.ruling: ἀνεπίφθονος = 'not envied/enviable', not 'inexhaustible'; 'no one envies' misrepresents passive/adjectival sense.

edits.old: Poverty is the root of love of money and is itself the root of freedom from love of money
edits.new: Poverty is the uprooting of love of money and the root of freedom from love of money

edits.old: It is radiant with love and shines together with patience
edits.new: It casts its vote with love and shares its vote with patience

fixed: a swift-running contestant: source ὀξύδρομος ἀγωνιστής means fierce combatant, not swift-running contestant
Poverty is the root of love of money: source φιλαργυρίας ἐκρίζωμα means uprooting of love of money, not root of love of money
radiant with love and shines together with patience: source ἀγάπης ἔμψηφος, καὶ μακροθυμίας σύμψηφος means casting vote with love and sharing vote with patience
a treasure no one envies: source ἀνεπίφθονος θησαυρὸς means inexhaustible treasure, not treasure no one envies
It does good to those who grieve it: source λυποῦσιν εὐποιΐα means doing good to those who cause grief; English is acceptable as is

problems.quote: It casts its vote with love
problems.why: Greek says “bright with love”, not “casts its vote”.
Greek means “wrath of the proud/arrogant”, not “wrath of insults”.
ὀξύδρομος means swift-footed, not fierce; ἀγωνιστής means athlete/contestant, not combatant.
problems.ruling: ὀξύδρομος = swift‑footed, not fierce; ἀγωνιστής = fighter, not necessarily fierce

problems.quote: It does good to those who grieve it
problems.why: λυποῦσιν is dative plural 'to those who cause grief/grieve others' or 'to those who are grieved'; the English 'those who grieve it' makes patience the object, but Greek likely means 'to those who grieve [others]'.
problems.fix: doing good to those who grieve others
problems.ruling: λύποῦσιν εὐποιΐα means 'good to the grieving', not 'those who grieve it'

problems.quote: and shares its vote with patience
problems.why: Greek says “bright with patience”, not “shares its vote”.
problems.ruling: σύμψηφος means 'co-voting/sharing vote'; μακροθυμίας is genitive 'of patience'

edits.old: It casts its vote with love and shares its vote with patience.
edits.new: It is bright with love and bright with patience.

edits.old: It does good to those who grieve it
edits.new: It does good to those who grieve others

fixed: ἀγάπης ἔμψηφος: corrected to 'It is bright with love' (ἔμψηφος means 'bright, radiant', not 'casting a vote').
μακροθυμίας σύμψηφος: corrected to 'bright with patience' (σύμψηφος means 'bright together with', not 'sharing a vote').
ὕβρεων μῆνις: corrected to 'a wrath of the proud' (ὕβρεων is genitive plural of ὕβρις, meaning 'of the arrogant/proud', not 'of insults').
ὀξύδρομος ἀγωνιστής: corrected to 'a swift-footed athlete' (ὀξύδρομος means 'swift-running', ἀγωνιστής means 'contestant/athlete', not 'fierce combatant').
λυποῦσιν εὐποιΐα: corrected to 'It does good to those who grieve others' (λυποῦσιν is dative plural, meaning 'to those who cause grief', not 'to those who grieve it').

problems.why: ἀνεπίφθονος means 'unenvied' or 'free from envy,' not 'inexhaustible' (apparently confused with ἄφθονος).
ὕβρεων is the genitive plural of ὕβρις ('insults,' 'outrages,' 'insolence'), not 'the proud.'

problems.quote: It is bright with love and bright with patience.
problems.why: ἔμψηφος and σύμψηφος derive from ψῆφος ('vote') and mean 'in agreement with' or 'of one mind with,' not 'bright.'
problems.fix: It is in agreement with love and of one mind with patience.
problems.ruling: ἔμψηφος and σύμψηφος (ψῆφος) imply agreement with love and patience, not brightness.

problems.quote: a mirror for those who hope
problems.why: ἐλπιζομένων is a passive neuter participle ('things hoped for,' cf. Heb 11:1), not active ἐλπιζόντων ('those who hope').
problems.fix: a mirror of the things hoped for
problems.ruling: ἐλπιζομένων is passive participle, things hoped for, not active ἐλπιζόντων, those who hope.

edits.old: It is bright with love and bright with patience.
edits.new: It is in agreement with love and of one mind with patience.

edits.old: a mirror for those who hope
edits.new: a mirror of the things hoped for

fixed: ἀνεπίφθονος θησαυρὸς: 'inexhaustible' (= ἄφθονος) corrected to 'treasure free from envy' (unenvied).
ὕβρεων μῆνις: genitive plural of ὕβρις ('insults') corrected from 'of the proud' to 'of insults'.
ἀγάπης ἔμψηφος, καὶ μακροθυμίας σύμψηφος: from ψῆφος ('vote') corrected from 'bright' to 'in agreement / of one mind'.
ἐλπιζομένων ἔσοπτρον: passive 'things hoped for' (cf. Hebrews 11:1) corrected from active 'those who hope' to 'of the things hoped for'.

problems.quote: a courtroom of the heart for anger. It is a place of healing
problems.why: Despite the misplaced comma in the edition, καρδίας pairs with ἰατρεῖον (matching the surrounding genitive-noun pairs), not with δικαστήριον.
problems.fix: a courtroom for anger, a place of healing for the heart
problems.ruling: Pattern pairs ὀργῆς with δικαστήριον and καρδίας with ἰατρεῖον; English joins καρδίας to court and drops heart from healing.

edits.old: a weapon of prudence and a courtroom of the heart for anger. It is a place of healing,
edits.new: a weapon of prudence, a courtroom for anger, and a place of healing for the heart,

fixed: Fixed courtroom/healing pairing: source has ὀργῆς δικαστήριον / καρδίας ἰατρεῖον, so heart belongs with healing, not with courtroom.

problems.quote: does good to those who grieve others
problems.why: Greek dative means those who grieve or hurt you, not people who sadden third parties.
problems.fix: does good to those who grieve us, or to those who cause grief
problems.ruling: In μακροθυμία, λυποῦσιν εὐποιΐα means doing good to those who hurt or grieve one, not third parties; adding 'others' misleads the reader.

edits.old: It does good to those who grieve others
edits.new: It does good to those who cause grief

fixed: Fixed `does good to those who grieve others`: source λυποῦσιν εὐποἰα is active causing grief to the patient, not grieving third parties — changed to `those who cause grief`.

refereed.why: Greek means “accusation of excess/overreaching”, not irritation.
refereed.ruling: παροξυσμοῦ = 'irritation/paroxysm' is valid; but ἔγκλημα = 'accusation/charge', not 'of irritation'—genitive is objective: 'accusation brought by irritation' or 'charge of paroxysm'. The English 'accusation of irritation' misrepresents the Greek syntax and meaning.

refereed.quote: does good to those who grieve others
refereed.why: Greek says “does good to those who grieve”, without “others”.
refereed.fix: does good to those who grieve
refereed.ruling: λυποῦσιν is dative plural 'to those who grieve' (passive/reflexive sense); adding 'others' changes meaning to active 'those who cause grief'.
